```{r cbt-triplet-timecourse-descriptive-stats}
# Combine all triplet data for the unified table
triplets_all_list <- c("DDD", "DDB", "DBD", "DBB", "BDD", "BDB", "BBD", "BBB")

df_all_triplets_cbt_unified <- data.frame()

for(triplet_type in triplets_all_list) {
  df_triplet_cbt <- data.frame()
  
  for(p in participants_noP07) {
    sessions_3 <- get_triplet_session3(p, triplet_type)
    
    if(length(sessions_3) > 0) {
      group_id <- get_group_id(p)
      session_ids <- paste0(group_id, sprintf("%02d", sessions_3))
      
      p_data <- cbt %>%
        filter(id == p, session %in% session_ids) %>%
        select(id, session, time_block, cbt_30min) %>%
        filter(!is.na(time_block)) %>%
        group_by(session, time_block) %>%
        slice(1) %>%
        ungroup() %>%
        mutate(triplet = triplet_type)
      
      df_triplet_cbt <- rbind(df_triplet_cbt, p_data)
    }
  }
  
  # Assign block numbers
  df_triplet_cbt <- df_triplet_cbt %>%
    group_by(id, session) %>%
    arrange(time_block) %>%
    mutate(block_num = row_number()) %>%
    ungroup()
  
  df_all_triplets_cbt_unified <- rbind(df_all_triplets_cbt_unified, df_triplet_cbt)
}

# Calculate summary statistics per triplet and block
triplet_summary_cbt_unified <- df_all_triplets_cbt_unified %>%
  group_by(triplet, block_num) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_cbt = mean(cbt_30min, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_cbt = sd(cbt_30min, na.rm = TRUE),
    n = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(triplet = factor(triplet, levels = triplets_all_list))

# Create table with mean ± SD for all triplets
triplet_timecourse_cbt_table <- triplet_summary_cbt_unified %>%
  mutate(
    mean_sd = sprintf("%.2f ± %.2f", mean_cbt, sd_cbt)
  ) %>%
  select(triplet, block_num, mean_sd) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = block_num,
    values_from = mean_sd,
    names_prefix = "B"
  )

knitr::kable(
  triplet_timecourse_cbt_table,
  caption = "Triplet time-course: Mean ± SD core body temperature (°C) per 30-minute block",
  align = c("l", rep("r", 10))
) %>%
  kableExtra::kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"), 
                           full_width = FALSE) %>%
  kableExtra::row_spec(0, bold = TRUE)
```

### Grand Average Time Course CBT

```{r cbt-timecourse-grand-average-preparation}
# Map light conditions to each session for CBT
light_patterns <- list(
  P01 = c("D", "D", "D", "B", "B", "B", "D", "D", "B", "D", "B"),
  P02 = c("D", "D", "D", "B", "B", "B", "D", "D", "B", "D", "B"),
  P03 = c("D", "D", "D", "B", "B", "B", "D", "D", "B", "D", "B"),
  P04 = c("D", "B", "B", "B", "D", "D", "D", "B", "D", "B"),
  P05 = c("D", "B", "B", "B", "D", "D", "D", "B", "D", "B"),
  P06 = c("D", "B", "B", "B", "D", "D", "D", "B", "D", "B"),
  P07 = c("D", "B", "B", "B", "D", "D", "D", "B", "D", "B"),
  P09 = c("D", "B", "B", "B", "D", "D", "D", "B", "D", "B")
)

# Add P10 pattern (12 sessions without session 5)
light_patterns[["P10"]] <- c("D", "D", "D", "B", "D", "B", "B", "B", "D", "B", "D", "D")

df_light_cbt <- bind_rows(
  # All participants except P10
  bind_rows(lapply(names(light_patterns), function(p) {
    pattern <- light_patterns[[p]]
    data.frame(
      id = p,
      exp_session = seq_along(pattern),
      light = pattern,
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
  })),
  # P10 
  data.frame(
    id = "P10",
    exp_session = 1:13,
    light = ifelse(1:13 %in% c(1,2,3,6,10,12,13), "D", "B"),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
)

# Add group information and create session IDs
df_light_cbt <- df_light_cbt %>%
  mutate(
    group = case_when(
      id %in% c("P01", "P02", "P03") ~ 1,
      id %in% c("P04", "P05") ~ 2,
      id %in% c("P06", "P07", "P09") ~ 3,
      id == "P10" ~ 4
    ),
    session = paste0(group, sprintf("%02d", exp_session))
  )

# Join with CBT data - get one row per session and time_block
df_cbt_light <- cbt %>%
  filter(id %in% c("P01", "P02", "P03", "P04", "P05", "P06", "P07", "P09", "P10")) %>%
  filter(!is.na(time_block)) %>%
  group_by(id, session, time_block) %>%
  slice(1) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  inner_join(df_light_cbt, by = c("id", "session"))

# Assign block numbers (1-10)
df_cbt_light <- df_cbt_light %>%
  group_by(id, session) %>%
  arrange(time_block) %>%
  mutate(block_num = row_number()) %>%
  ungroup()

# Calculate per-participant summary
df_summary_cbt_per_participant <- df_cbt_light %>%
  group_by(id, block_num, light) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_cbt = mean(cbt_30min, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_cbt = sd(cbt_30min, na.rm = TRUE),
    n = n(),
    se_cbt = sd_cbt / sqrt(n),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(light = factor(light, levels = c("D", "B"), labels = c("Dim", "Bright")))

# Grand average excluding P07
df_summary_cbt_noP07 <- df_summary_cbt_per_participant %>%
  filter(id != "P07")

grand_summary_cbt_manual <- data.frame()

for(b in unique(df_summary_cbt_noP07$block_num)) {
  for(l in levels(df_summary_cbt_noP07$light)) {
    vals <- df_summary_cbt_noP07 %>%
      filter(block_num == b, light == l) %>%
      pull(mean_cbt)
    
    n_val <- length(vals)
    mean_val <- mean(vals, na.rm = TRUE)
    sd_val <- sd(vals, na.rm = TRUE)
    se_val <- sd_val / sqrt(n_val)
    
    grand_summary_cbt_manual <- rbind(grand_summary_cbt_manual, data.frame(
      block_num = b,
      light = l,
      mean_cbt = mean_val,
      sd_cbt = sd_val,
      n = n_val,
      se_cbt = se_val
    ))
  }
}

grand_summary_cbt_manual$light <- factor(grand_summary_cbt_manual$light, 
                                         levels = c("Bright", "Dim"))
```

```{r cbt-timecourse-grand-average-plot}
# Ensure block_num is numeric
grand_summary_cbt_manual <- grand_summary_cbt_manual %>%
  mutate(block_num = as.numeric(block_num))

# Define labels
hbt_values <- c("5.25", "4.75", "4.25", "3.75", "3.25", "2.75", "2.25", "1.75", "1.25", "0.75")

# Create x-axis labels
x_labels <- sapply(1:10, function(i) {
  if (i %% 2 == 1) {  
    paste0("B", i, "\n(", hbt_values[i], "h)")
  } else {  
    paste0("B", i)
  }
})

# Y-axis limits
y_min <- floor(min(grand_summary_cbt_manual$mean_cbt - grand_summary_cbt_manual$se_cbt, 
                   na.rm = TRUE) * 10) / 10 - 0.1
y_max <- ceiling(max(grand_summary_cbt_manual$mean_cbt + grand_summary_cbt_manual$se_cbt, 
                     na.rm = TRUE) * 10) / 10 + 0.1

# Create plot
ggplot(grand_summary_cbt_manual, 
       aes(x = block_num, y = mean_cbt, 
           color = light, fill = light, group = light)) +
  # Background shading
  annotate("rect", xmin = 0.5, xmax = 6.5, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, 
           fill = "#F5F5F5", alpha = 0.4) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = 6.5, xmax = 9.5, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, 
           fill = "#FFF9E6", alpha = 0.8) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = 9.5, xmax = 10.5, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, 
           fill = "#F5F5F5", alpha = 0.4) +
  annotate("text", x = 3.75, y = y_max - 0.02, label = "dim\n(10 lx)",  
           hjust = 0.5, vjust = 1, size = 3.5, color = "grey50", fontface = "italic") +
  annotate("text", x = 8, y = y_max - 0.02, label = "intervention\n(10 or 1000 lx)",  
           hjust = 0.5, vjust = 1, size = 3.5, color = "#B8860B", fontface = "italic") +
  annotate("text", x = 10, y = y_max - 0.02, label = "dim\n(10 lx)", 
           hjust = 0.5, vjust = 1, size = 3.5, color = "grey50", fontface = "italic") + 
  # Ribbon for SE
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = mean_cbt - se_cbt,
                  ymax = mean_cbt + se_cbt),
              alpha = 0.1, color = NA, show.legend = FALSE) +
  # Line and points
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(size = 3.5, shape = 16) +
  # Colors
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c("Bright" = "#F5A623", "Dim" = "#4A90E2"),
    labels = c("Bright" = "Bright (1000 lx)", "Dim" = "Dim (10 lx)")
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("Bright" = "#F5A623", "Dim" = "#4A90E2"),
    labels = c("Bright" = "Bright (1000 lx)", "Dim" = "Dim (10 lx)")
  ) +
  # Axes 
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = 1:10,
    labels = x_labels,
    limits = c(0.5, 10.5),
    expand = c(0, 0)
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(y_min, y_max), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  # Labels
  labs(
    title = "Core body temperature time course",
    subtitle = "Grand average across participants (P07 excluded, n=8)",
    x = "30-minute block (hours before HBT)",
    y = "Mean Core Body Temperature (°C)",
    color = "Light condition",
    fill = "Light condition"
  ) +
  # Theme
  theme_classic(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    aspect.ratio = 1,
    plot.title = element_text(size = 16, hjust = 0),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 13, hjust = 0, margin = margin(b = 10)),
    axis.text = element_text(color = "black", size = 13),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 9, margin = margin(t = 5)),  # ← KLEINER + ABSTAND
    axis.title = element_text(size = 14),
    axis.title.x = element_text(margin = margin(t = 12)),  # ← MEHR ABSTAND
    axis.title.y = element_text(margin = margin(r = 8)),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(color = "grey90", linewidth = 0.3),
    legend.position = "right",
    plot.margin = margin(15, 10, 10, 10)
  )
```

### Panel View Triplet and Grand Average Time Courses

```{r cbt-triplet-grand-average-combined}
#| label: fig-cbt-triplet-panel
#| fig-cap: "Core body temperature time course - Grand average and triplet patterns (P07 excluded)"
#| fig-width: 14
#| fig-height: 8

# 1. Prepare data for all triplets
triplets_all_panel <- c("DDD", "BDD", "DBD", "BBD", "DDB", "BDB", "DBB", "BBB")

df_all_triplets_cbt_for_panel <- data.frame()

for(triplet_type in triplets_all_panel) {
  df_triplet_cbt <- data.frame()
  
  for(p in participants_noP07) {
    sessions_3 <- get_triplet_session3(p, triplet_type)
    
    if(length(sessions_3) > 0) {
      group_id <- get_group_id(p)
      session_ids <- paste0(group_id, sprintf("%02d", sessions_3))
      
      p_data <- cbt %>%
        filter(id == p, session %in% session_ids) %>%
        select(id, session, time_block, cbt_30min) %>%
        filter(!is.na(time_block)) %>%
        group_by(session, time_block) %>%
        slice(1) %>%
        ungroup() %>%
        mutate(triplet = triplet_type)
      
      df_triplet_cbt <- rbind(df_triplet_cbt, p_data)
    }
  }
  
  df_triplet_cbt <- df_triplet_cbt %>%
    group_by(id, session) %>%
    arrange(time_block) %>%
    mutate(block_num = row_number()) %>%
    ungroup()
  
  df_all_triplets_cbt_for_panel <- rbind(df_all_triplets_cbt_for_panel, df_triplet_cbt)
}

# 2. Calculate summary per triplet
triplet_summary_cbt_for_panel <- df_all_triplets_cbt_for_panel %>%
  group_by(triplet, block_num) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_cbt = mean(cbt_30min, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_cbt = sd(cbt_30min, na.rm = TRUE),
    n = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    triplet = factor(triplet, levels = triplets_all_panel),
    triplet_type = ifelse(substr(triplet, 3, 3) == "D", "Dim", "Bright")
  )

# 3. Unified Y-axis limits
y_min_cbt_unified <- floor(min(triplet_summary_cbt_for_panel$mean_cbt - triplet_summary_cbt_for_panel$sd_cbt, 
                               na.rm = TRUE) * 10) / 10 - 0.1
y_max_cbt_unified <- ceiling(max(triplet_summary_cbt_for_panel$mean_cbt + triplet_summary_cbt_for_panel$sd_cbt, 
                                 na.rm = TRUE) * 10) / 10 + 0.1

# 4. Function to create triplet plot
create_triplet_plot_cbt <- function(triplet_name, show_x = FALSE, show_y = TRUE) {
  data_triplet <- triplet_summary_cbt_for_panel %>%
    filter(triplet == triplet_name)
  
  triplet_third <- substr(triplet_name, 3, 3)
  intervention_color <- ifelse(triplet_third == "D", "#F5F5F5", "#FFF9E6")
  intervention_alpha <- ifelse(triplet_third == "D", 0.4, 0.8)
  
  triplet_first_two <- substr(triplet_name, 1, 2)
  triplet_label <- paste0(triplet_first_two, "**", triplet_third, "**")
  
  x_labels_with_hbt <- c(
    "B1\n(5.25h)", "B2", "B3\n(4.25h)", "B4", "B5\n(3.25h)", 
    "B6", "B7\n(2.25h)", "B8", "B9\n(1.25h)", "B10"
  )
  
  ggplot(data_triplet, aes(x = block_num, y = mean_cbt)) +
    annotate("rect", xmin = 0.5, xmax = 6.5, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, 
             fill = "#F5F5F5", alpha = 0.4) +
    annotate("rect", xmin = 6.5, xmax = 9.5, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, 
             fill = intervention_color, alpha = intervention_alpha) +
    annotate("rect", xmin = 9.5, xmax = 10.5, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, 
             fill = "#F5F5F5", alpha = 0.4) +
    geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = mean_cbt - sd_cbt, 
                    ymax = mean_cbt + sd_cbt),
                alpha = 0.15, fill = "grey40") +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.8, color = "black") +
    geom_point(size = 2.5, shape = 16, color = "black") +
    scale_x_continuous(
      breaks = 1:10,
      labels = if(show_x) x_labels_with_hbt else 1:10,
      limits = c(0.5, 10.5),
      expand = c(0, 0)
    ) +
    scale_y_continuous(limits = c(y_min_cbt_unified, y_max_cbt_unified), expand = c(0, 0)) +
    labs(
      title = triplet_label,
      x = NULL,
      y = if(show_y) "Mean core body\ntemperature ± SD (°C)" else NULL
    ) +
    theme_classic(base_size = 11) +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_markdown(size = 11, hjust = 0.5, margin = margin(b = 5)),
      axis.text = element_text(color = "black", size = 9),
      axis.text.x = element_text(size = if(show_x) 7 else 8, margin = margin(t = 3)),
      axis.title = element_text(size = 10),
      axis.title.y = element_text(margin = margin(r = 5)),
      panel.grid.major.y = element_line(color = "grey90", linewidth = 0.3),
      plot.margin = margin(5, 5, if(show_x) 8 else 5, 5)
    )
}

# 5. Create D-ending triplet plots (no x-axis labels)
p_DDD_cbt <- create_triplet_plot_cbt("DDD", show_x = FALSE, show_y = TRUE)
p_BDD_cbt <- create_triplet_plot_cbt("BDD", show_x = FALSE, show_y = FALSE)
p_DBD_cbt <- create_triplet_plot_cbt("DBD", show_x = FALSE, show_y = FALSE)
p_BBD_cbt <- create_triplet_plot_cbt("BBD", show_x = FALSE, show_y = FALSE)

# 6. Create B-ending triplet plots (with x-axis labels)
p_DDB_cbt <- create_triplet_plot_cbt("DDB", show_x = TRUE, show_y = TRUE)
p_BDB_cbt <- create_triplet_plot_cbt("BDB", show_x = TRUE, show_y = FALSE)
p_DBB_cbt <- create_triplet_plot_cbt("DBB", show_x = TRUE, show_y = FALSE)
p_BBB_cbt <- create_triplet_plot_cbt("BBB", show_x = TRUE, show_y = FALSE)

# 7. Grand Average plot
p_grand_cbt <- ggplot(grand_summary_cbt_manual,
       aes(x = block_num, y = mean_cbt,
           color = light, fill = light, group = light)) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = 0.5, xmax = 6.5, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,
           fill = "#F5F5F5", alpha = 0.4) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = 9.5, xmax = 10.5, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,
           fill = "#F5F5F5", alpha = 0.4) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = 6.5, xmax = 9.5, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,
           fill = "#FFF9E6", alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = mean_cbt - se_cbt,
                  ymax = mean_cbt + se_cbt),
              alpha = 0.1, color = NA, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5, shape = 16) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c("Bright" = "#F5A623", "Dim" = "#4A90E2"),
    labels = c("Bright" = "Bright (1000lx)", "Dim" = "Dim (10lx)")
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("Bright" = "#F5A623", "Dim" = "#4A90E2"),
    labels = c("Bright" = "Bright (1000lx)", "Dim" = "Dim (10lx)")
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = 1:10,
    labels = 1:10,
    limits = c(0.5, 10.5),
    expand = c(0, 0)
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(y_min_cbt_unified, y_max_cbt_unified), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  labs(
    title = "Grand Average",
    x = NULL,
    y = NULL,
    color = "Light condition"
  ) +
  guides(
    color = guide_legend(override.aes = list(shape = 16, size = 2.5)),
    fill = "none"
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 11, hjust = 0.5, margin = margin(b = 5)),
    axis.text = element_text(color = "black", size = 9),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 8, margin = margin(t = 3)),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 10),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(color = "grey90", linewidth = 0.3),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.title = element_text(size = 9),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 7),
    plot.margin = margin(5, 5, 5, 5)
  )

# 8. Empty spacer
p_spacer <- ggplot() + theme_void()

# 9. Combine in layout
(p_DDD_cbt | p_BDD_cbt | p_DBD_cbt | p_BBD_cbt | p_grand_cbt) /
(p_DDB_cbt | p_BDB_cbt | p_DBB_cbt | p_BBB_cbt | p_spacer) +
  plot_annotation(
    title = "Core body temperature time course - Grand average and triplet patterns",
    subtitle = "Grand average and third-day triplet patterns (P07 excluded)",
    caption = "30-minute block (hours before HBT)",
    theme = theme(
      plot.title = element_text(size = 15, hjust = 0, face = "plain"),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 12, hjust = 0, margin = margin(b = 8)),
      plot.caption = element_text(size = 11, hjust = 0.5, margin = margin(t = 10))
    )
  )
```

# Data Preparation for CBT Statistical Analysis

## Define Study Parameters for CBT

```{r cbt-data-prep}
# Define participant list and light patterns
participant_list <- c("P01", "P02", "P03", "P04", "P05", "P06", "P07", "P09", "P10")

# Combine CBT data with light information
cbt_lmm <- map_dfr(participant_list, ~{
  df <- cbt %>% 
    filter(id == .x) %>%
    # Extract session number from session variable (e.g., "101" -> 1, "102" -> 2)
    mutate(exp_session = as.integer(substr(session, 2, 3))) %>%
    # Keep only cbt_intervention values (one per session)
    filter(!is.na(cbt_intervention)) %>%
    distinct(id, exp_session, cbt_intervention, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
    select(id, exp_session, cbt_intervention) %>%
    rename(participant_id = id)
  
  # Special light pattern assignment for P10 (missing session 5)
  if(.x == "P10") {
    # Manual assignment for each actual session number
    light_df <- tibble(
      exp_session = c(1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13),
      Light_Lag0 = c("D", "D", "D", "B", "D", "B", "B", "B", "D", "B", "D", "D")
    )
  } else {
    light_df <- tibble(
      exp_session = seq_along(light_patterns[[.x]]),
      Light_Lag0 = light_patterns[[.x]]
    )
  }
  
  df <- df %>% 
    left_join(light_df, by = "exp_session")
  
  return(df)
})

# Build lagged light variables and filter valid triplets
cbt_lmm <- cbt_lmm %>%
  group_by(participant_id) %>%
  arrange(exp_session) %>%
  mutate(
    Light_Lag1 = lag(Light_Lag0, 1),
    Light_Lag2 = lag(Light_Lag0, 2)
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(!is.na(Light_Lag0) & !is.na(Light_Lag1) & !is.na(Light_Lag2)) %>%
  filter(!(participant_id == "P10" & exp_session %in% c(6, 7))) %>%
  mutate(
    Light_Lag0_num = ifelse(Light_Lag0 == "D", 0, 1),
    Light_Lag1_num = ifelse(Light_Lag1 == "D", 0, 1),
    Light_Lag2_num = ifelse(Light_Lag2 == "D", 0, 1)
  )

# Add participant demographics (including BMI)
participant_demographics_cbt <- tibble(
  participant_id = c("P01", "P02", "P03", "P04", "P05", "P06", "P07", "P09", "P10"),
  sex = c("female", "male", "female", "female", "male", "female", "female", "female", "male"),
  age = c(24, 21, 24, 23, 31, 23, 24, 28, 32),
  bmi = c(25.82645, 18.83239, 28.01022, 24.67550, 20.28651, 22.23099, 23.23346, 24.50895, 27.14304)
)

cbt_lmm <- cbt_lmm %>%
  left_join(participant_demographics_cbt, by = "participant_id")

# Apply exclusion criteria
cbt_lmm <- cbt_lmm %>%
  filter(participant_id != "P07")  # Exclude P07 (consistent with melatonin analysis)

# Keep only necessary variables
cbt_lmm <- cbt_lmm %>%
  dplyr::select(
    participant_id, exp_session, cbt_intervention,
    Light_Lag0, Light_Lag1, Light_Lag2,
    Light_Lag0_num, Light_Lag1_num, Light_Lag2_num,
    sex, age, bmi
  )
```

# Statistical Analysis for Core Body Temperature

## Model Building Strategy

### Model m0: Baseline (Random Intercept Only)

This baseline model quantifies between-participant variability without any predictors.

```{r cbt-m0}
m0_cbt <- lmer(
  cbt_intervention ~ 1 + (1 | participant_id),
  data = cbt_lmm,
  REML = FALSE
)

summary(m0_cbt)

# Wald Confidence Intervals
ci_m0 <- confint(m0_cbt, method = "Wald")
print(ci_m0)
```

### Model m1a: Add Light Lag 0 (Current Day)

This model adds the current day light exposure variable as a fixed effect with Light_Lag0_num.

```{r cbt-m1a}
m1a_cbt <- lmer(
  cbt_intervention ~ 
    Light_Lag0_num +
    (1 | participant_id),
  data = cbt_lmm,
  REML = FALSE
)

summary(m1a_cbt)

# Wald Confidence Intervals
ci_m1a <- confint(m1a_cbt, method = "Wald")
print(ci_m1a)
```

### Model m1b: Add Light Lag 1 Additionally (One Day Before)

This model adds the day before light exposure variable as a fixed effect with Light_Lag1_num.

```{r cbt-m1b}
m1b_cbt <- lmer(
  cbt_intervention ~ 
    Light_Lag0_num + Light_Lag1_num +
    (1 | participant_id),
  data = cbt_lmm,
  REML = FALSE
)

summary(m1b_cbt)

# Wald Confidence Intervals
ci_m1b <- confint(m1b_cbt, method = "Wald")
print(ci_m1b)
```

### Model m1c: Add Light Lag 2 Additionally (Two Days Before)

This model adds the light exposure two days before as a fixed effect with Light_Lag2_num.

```{r cbt-m1c}
m1c_cbt <- lmer(
  cbt_intervention ~ 
    Light_Lag0_num + Light_Lag1_num + Light_Lag2_num +
    (1 | participant_id),
  data = cbt_lmm,
  REML = FALSE
)

summary(m1c_cbt)

# Wald Confidence Intervals
ci_m1c <- confint(m1c_cbt, method = "Wald")
print(ci_m1c)
```

### Likelihood Ratio Tests: Lag Effects

```{r cbt-lrt-lags}
# LRT 1: Does adding Lag 0 improve fit over baseline?
lrt_m0_vs_m1a_cbt <- anova(m0_cbt, m1a_cbt)

# LRT 2: Does adding Lag 1 improve fit over Lag 0 only?
lrt_m1a_vs_m1b_cbt <- anova(m1a_cbt, m1b_cbt)

# LRT 3: Does adding Lag 2 improve fit over Lag 0 + Lag 1?
lrt_m1b_vs_m1c_cbt <- anova(m1b_cbt, m1c_cbt)

# Display results
lrt_m0_vs_m1a_cbt
lrt_m1a_vs_m1b_cbt
lrt_m1b_vs_m1c_cbt
```

### Model m2: Add Linear Session Effect

This model adds a linear session term to account for potential temporal trends across the study.

```{r cbt-m2-session}
m2_cbt <- lmer(
  cbt_intervention ~ 
    exp_session +
    (1 | participant_id),
  data = cbt_lmm,
  REML = FALSE
)

summary(m2_cbt)

# Wald Confidence Intervals
ci_m2 <- confint(m2_cbt, method = "Wald")
print(ci_m2)
```

### Model m3: Add Quadratic Session Effect

This model tests for non-linear temporal trends (e.g., U-shaped patterns) across sessions.

```{r cbt-m3-quadratic}
m3_cbt <- lmer(
  cbt_intervention ~ 
    exp_session + I(exp_session^2) +
    (1 | participant_id),
  data = cbt_lmm,
  REML = FALSE
)

summary(m3_cbt)

# Wald Confidence Intervals
ci_m3 <- confint(m3_cbt, method = "Wald")
print(ci_m3)
```

### Likelihood Ratio Tests: Session Effects

```{r cbt-lrt-session-effects}
# LRT 1: Does adding exp_session (linear) improve fit over baseline?
lrt_m0_vs_m2_cbt <- anova(m0_cbt, m2_cbt)

# LRT 2: Does adding quadratic term improve fit over linear only?
lrt_m2_vs_m3_cbt <- anova(m2_cbt, m3_cbt)

lrt_m0_vs_m2_cbt
lrt_m2_vs_m3_cbt
```

## Model Selection Summary

Model m2 (cbt_intervention \~ exp_session + (1 \| participant_id)) was chosen as the final model due to the following LRT results:

-   Lag 0 (Current day light): Adding Lag 0 did not significantly improve fit over random intercept model only (m0 vs. m1a: χ²=0.9998, p=0.317)

-   Lag 1 (Previous day): Adding Lag 1 did not significantly improve fit over model m1a (m1a vs. m1b: χ²=0.281, p=0.596)

-   Lag 2 (Two days prior): Adding Lag 2 did not significantly improve model fit over model m1b (m1b vs. m1c: χ²=2.076, p=0.150)

-   Linear session effect: Adding a linear session term did significantly improve model fit over model m0 (m0 vs. m2: χ²=4.794, p=0.029)

-   Quadratic session effect: Adding a quadratic session term did not significantly improve model fit over model m2 (m2 vs. m3: χ²=0.204, p=0.651)

Therefore a model only using the experimental session number as the fixed effect and participant id as the random intercept was selected as the final model. Model m2 unadjusted values are: Each additional experimental day is associated with an average increase of approximately 0.019°C in core body temperature (p=0.029).

## Model Diagnostics

### Check 1: Multicollinearity (VIF)

```{r cbt-check1-vif}
# Note: Model m2_cbt contains only one predictor (exp_session)
# VIF is not applicable for single-predictor models
print(formula(m2_cbt))
```

**Interpretation Check 1 - VIF:**

VIF (Variance Inflation Factor) is not applicable as the final model (m2_cbt) contains only a single fixed effect predictor (exp_session). Multicollinearity can only occur with multiple predictors, therefore this diagnostic check is not relevant for the current model.

### Check 2: Residual Plots

```{r cbt-check2-residuals}
# First calculate Cook's D 
infl_m2_cbt_check2 <- influence(m2_cbt, obs = TRUE)
cooks_d_cbt_check2 <- cooks.distance(infl_m2_cbt_check2)
threshold_cbt_check2 <- 4/nrow(cbt_lmm)

par(mfrow = c(2, 2))

# 1. Residuals vs Fitted
plot(fitted(m2_cbt), resid(m2_cbt), 
     xlab = "Fitted", ylab = "Residuals",
     main = "Residuals vs Fitted", pch = 16, col = rgb(0, 0, 0, 0.5))
abline(h = 0, col = "red", lty = 2, lwd = 2)
lines(lowess(fitted(m2_cbt), resid(m2_cbt)), col = "blue", lwd = 2)

# 2. Q-Q Plot
qqnorm(resid(m2_cbt), main = "Q-Q Plot", pch = 16, col = rgb(0, 0, 0, 0.5))
qqline(resid(m2_cbt), col = "red", lwd = 2)

# 3. Scale-Location
plot(fitted(m2_cbt), sqrt(abs(resid(m2_cbt))), 
     xlab = "Fitted", ylab = "√|Residuals|",
     main = "Scale-Location", pch = 16, col = rgb(0, 0, 0, 0.5))
lines(lowess(fitted(m2_cbt), sqrt(abs(resid(m2_cbt)))), col = "blue", lwd = 2)

# 4. Cook's Distance
plot(cooks_d_cbt_check2, type = "h", main = "Cook's Distance",
     ylab = "Cook's D", lwd = 2,
     col = ifelse(cooks_d_cbt_check2 > threshold_cbt_check2, "red", "black"))
abline(h = threshold_cbt_check2, col = "red", lty = 2, lwd = 2)

par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```

**Interpretation Check 2 - Residual Plots:**

-   **Residuals vs. Fitted plot:** Residuals show no strong systematic pattern around the zero line, with the LOESS smoother remaining approximately horizontal. Both linearity and homogeneity of variance assumption appear to be satisfied.
-   **QQ Plot:** Despite good fit in the central regions of the plot, some deviation in the lower and upper tail are visible, which are typical for a smaller sample size and do not substantially threaten the normality assumption.\
-   **Scale-Location Plot:** Visual inspection reveals no strong systematic patterns in variance across fitted values. The slight curvature in the LOESS smoother is likely attributable to the limited sample size. The homogeneity of variance assumption seems to be satisfied.
-   **Cook's Distance Plot:** 3 values above the n/4 threshold were identified using the influence.ME package are identified. Those values will be excluded during a sensitivity analysis (robust dataset) to identify whether those values drive the main effect of the experimental session number.

### Check 3: Normality (Shapiro-Wilk)

```{r cbt-check3-normality}
# Shapiro-Wilk test for normality of residuals
shapiro_test_cbt <- shapiro.test(resid(m2_cbt))
print(shapiro_test_cbt)
```

**Interpretation Check 3 - Normality:**

Shapiro-Wilk test shows a statistically signficant deviation from normality assumotion for residuals (W=0.961, p=0.0346). Sensitivity analyses will be perofrmed to test results.

### Check 4: Heteroskedasticity (Levene's Test)

```{r cbt-check4-heteroskedasticity}
# Create plot for visual inspection
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))

plot(fitted(m2_cbt), resid(m2_cbt), 
     xlab = "Fitted", ylab = "Residuals",
     main = "Residuals vs Fitted", pch = 16, col = rgb(0, 0, 0, 0.5))
abline(h = 0, col = "red", lty = 2, lwd = 2)
lines(lowess(fitted(m2_cbt), resid(m2_cbt)), col = "blue", lwd = 2)

plot(fitted(m2_cbt), sqrt(abs(resid(m2_cbt))), 
     xlab = "Fitted", ylab = "√|Residuals|",
     main = "Scale-Location", pch = 16, col = rgb(0, 0, 0, 0.5))
lines(lowess(fitted(m2_cbt), sqrt(abs(resid(m2_cbt)))), col = "blue", lwd = 2)
abline(h = mean(sqrt(abs(resid(m2_cbt)))), col = "red", lty = 2, lwd = 2)

par(mfrow = c(1, 1))

# Levene's Test
fitted_groups_cbt <- cut(fitted(m2_cbt), 
                         breaks = quantile(fitted(m2_cbt), probs = c(0, 0.5, 1)),
                         include.lowest = TRUE)
levene_test_cbt <- leveneTest(resid(m2_cbt) ~ fitted_groups_cbt)
print(levene_test_cbt)
```

**Interpretation Check 4 - Heteroskedasticity:**

Levene's test revealed no evidence of heterogeneity of variance across groups, indicating that the assumption of homoscedasticity was met (F(1, 65) = 0.728, p = 0.397). Visual inspections of the residuals vs. fitted as well as the scale-location plot show visually some patterns of heterogeneity of variance.Especially the scale-location plot shows lower variance for fitted values around 37°C CBT and higher variance for values below or above.

### Check 5: Random Effects Normality

```{r cbt-check5-random-effects}
# Extract random effects
ranef_m2_cbt <- ranef(m2_cbt)$participant_id

par(mfrow = c(1, 2))

# Histogram of random intercepts
hist(ranef_m2_cbt$`(Intercept)`, main = "Random Intercepts",
     xlab = "Random Intercept", col = "lightblue", border = "black", breaks = 8)

# Q-Q Plot of random intercepts
qqnorm(ranef_m2_cbt$`(Intercept)`, main = "Q-Q Plot: Random Intercepts",
       pch = 16, col = rgb(0, 0, 0, 0.6))
qqline(ranef_m2_cbt$`(Intercept)`, col = "red", lwd = 2)

par(mfrow = c(1, 1))

# Shapiro-Wilk test for random effects
shapiro_re_cbt <- shapiro.test(ranef_m2_cbt$`(Intercept)`)
print(shapiro_re_cbt)
```

**Interpretation Check 5 - Random Effects Normality:**

Visual as well as formal evaluation of the normality of random intercepts (W = 0.931, p = 0.522) assumption shows no substantial violation of this assumption. However, it needs to be stressed that a sample size of n=8 limits the interpret ability of such tests.

### Check 6: Influential Observations

```{r cbt-check6-influential}
# Calculate Cook's Distance
infl_m2_cbt <- influence(m2_cbt, obs = TRUE)
cooks_d_cbt <- cooks.distance(infl_m2_cbt)
threshold_cbt <- 4/nrow(cbt_lmm)

# Plot Cook's Distance
plot(cooks_d_cbt, type = "h", main = "Cook's Distance - CBT Model m2",
     ylab = "Cook's D", lwd = 2,
     col = ifelse(cooks_d_cbt > threshold_cbt, "red", "black"))
abline(h = threshold_cbt, lty = 2, col = "red")

# Identify influential observations
influential_idx_cbt <- which(cooks_d_cbt > threshold_cbt)

cat("Number of influential observations:", length(influential_idx_cbt), 
    paste0("(", round(length(influential_idx_cbt)/nrow(cbt_lmm)*100, 1), "% of data)\n\n"))

if (length(influential_idx_cbt) > 0) {
  cat("Influential observations:\n")
  print(cbt_lmm[influential_idx_cbt, c("participant_id", "exp_session", "cbt_intervention")])
}
```

**Interpretation Check 6 - Influential Observations:**

3 influential observations were identified by calculating Cook´s distance using the threshold 4/n. The following values were identified as influential observations exceeding this threshold: P01, Session 3, CBT value 37; P10, Session 3, CBT value around 37.1°C; P03, Session 10, CBT value 36.8°C.

### Check 5: Temporal Autocorrelation

```{r}
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))

acf(resid(m2_cbt), main = "ACF: Residuals", lag.max = 13)
pacf(resid(m2_cbt), main = "PACF: Residuals", lag.max = 13)
```

```{r}
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```

**Interpretation Check 5 - Temporal Autocorrelation:**

Both the ACF and PACF plots show indication of temporal autocorrelation for Lag 4. This suggests that residuals are not fully independent across time, potentially violating the independence assumption of the linear mixed model. Thereofre, a senstivity analysis will be performed emplyoing an AR(1) structure.

### Diagnostic Summary

```{r}
# Create fitted value groups for Levene's test
fitted_groups_cbt <- cut(fitted(m2_cbt), 
                         breaks = 2, 
                         labels = c("Low", "High"))

# Extract random effects for normality test
ranef_m2_cbt <- ranef(m2_cbt)

# Perform diagnostic tests
shapiro_resid_cbt <- shapiro.test(resid(m2_cbt))
levene_result_cbt <- leveneTest(resid(m2_cbt) ~ fitted_groups_cbt)
shapiro_re_cbt <- shapiro.test(ranef_m2_cbt$participant_id[, "(Intercept)"])

print(shapiro_resid_cbt)
```

```{r}
print(levene_result_cbt)
```

```{r}
print(shapiro_re_cbt)
```

**Interpretation Diagnostic Summary:**

-   Shapiro-Wilk test for normality of residuals indicated evidence of a violation of the normality assumption for the residuals (W=0.9611, p=0.0346)
-   Levene's test revealed no evidence of heterogeneity of variance across groups, indicating that the assumption of homoscedasticity was sufficiently met (F(1, \[65\])= \[1.6123\], p=0.2087)
-   Shapiro-Wilk test for normality of random intercepts showed no evidence of a deviation from normality, though the limited statistical power of this test due to small number of random intercepts (n=8) should be acknowledged (W=0.9306, p=0.5215)

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Sensitivity Analyses

### Sensitivity Analysis: AR(1) Correlation Structure

```{r}
# Fit model with AR(1) correlation structure
m2_cbt_ar1 <- lme(
  fixed = cbt_intervention ~ exp_session,        
  random = ~ 1 | participant_id,                 
  correlation = corAR1(form = ~ exp_session | participant_id),
  data = cbt_lmm,
  method = "ML"                                  
)

summary(m2_cbt_ar1)

# AR(1) Model: Wald 95% CI
ar1_coefs <- summary(m2_cbt_ar1)$tTable
ar1_ci <- data.frame(
  Effect = rownames(ar1_coefs),
  Estimate = ar1_coefs[, "Value"],
  SE = ar1_coefs[, "Std.Error"],
  CI_lower = ar1_coefs[, "Value"] - 1.96 * ar1_coefs[, "Std.Error"],
  CI_upper = ar1_coefs[, "Value"] + 1.96 * ar1_coefs[, "Std.Error"],
  p_value = format.pval(ar1_coefs[, "p-value"], digits = 3, eps = 0.001)
)

print(ar1_ci)
```

Interpretation Sensitivity 1: Applying an autoregressive correlation structure to account for temporal dependencies resulted in the main effect of experimental session becoming non-significant (β=0.018, SE=0.01 p=0.070). The AR(1) parameter (Phi1 = 0.24) indicates slight to moderate positive autocorrelation between consecutive measurements within participants. To summarize, the main effect of experimental session number on core body temperature values was not robust when accounting for the detected temporal correlation patterns in the residuals. Therefore, this effect should be treated with caution and may be partially explained by autocorrelation in the data rather than a true linear trend.

### Alternative: AR(4) Correlation Structure

As there was an autocorrelation for Lag 4, an AR(4) structure will be tested:

```{r}
m2_cbt_ar4 <- lme(
  fixed = cbt_intervention ~ exp_session,
  random = ~ 1 | participant_id,
  correlation = corARMA(form = ~ exp_session | participant_id, p = 4, q = 0),
  data = cbt_lmm,
  method = "ML"
)

summary(m2_cbt_ar4)

# AR(4) Model: Wald 95% CI
ar4_coefs <- summary(m2_cbt_ar4)$tTable
ar4_ci <- data.frame(
  Effect = rownames(ar4_coefs),
  Estimate = ar4_coefs[, "Value"],
  SE = ar4_coefs[, "Std.Error"],
  CI_lower = ar4_coefs[, "Value"] - 1.96 * ar4_coefs[, "Std.Error"],
  CI_upper = ar4_coefs[, "Value"] + 1.96 * ar4_coefs[, "Std.Error"],
  p_value = format.pval(ar4_coefs[, "p-value"], digits = 3, eps = 0.001)
)

print(ar4_ci)
```

Interpretation Sensitivity 1: In this model,the main effect of experimental session was not robust when applying an autoregressive correlation structure of order 4 (β=0.018, SE=0.013, p=0.172). The Phi parameters do NOT indicate a monotonically decreasing correlation pattern: Phi1 (0.36) and Phi2 (0.33) show similar moderate correlations for lags 1-2, while Phi3 (0.09) and Phi4 (0.09) show weak correlations for lags 3-4. This non-monotonic pattern suggests an irregular temporal structure that may indicate model misspecification. However, the worsening of AIC values (-9.9 for AR4 vs. -13.9 for AR1) suggests that the AR(4) model is overfitting the data. Despite the AR(4) model being less parsimonious, the loss of significance of the main effect of experimental session on CBT values under both AR(1) and AR(4) structures indicates that the original finding should be interpreted with caution, as it appears sensitive to assumptions about temporal correlation.

### 13.3.3 Sensitivity Analysis: Robust Standard Errors

**Context:** To address the violation of normality assumption (Shapiro-Wilk p = 0.008) and potential heteroskedasticity, we re-estimated the primary model (m2_cbt) using cluster-robust standard errors (CR2 adjustment), which provide valid inference even under non-normality and heteroskedasticity.

```{r}
# Calculate robust standard errors (CR2 method)
robust_results_cbt <- coef_test(m2_cbt, vcov = "CR2")

# Display robust results
print(robust_results_cbt)

# Wald 95% CI 
robust_ci_full <- data.frame(
  Effect = robust_results_cbt$Coef,
  Estimate = robust_results_cbt$beta,
  SE = robust_results_cbt$SE,
  CI_lower = robust_results_cbt$beta - 1.96 * robust_results_cbt$SE,
  CI_upper = robust_results_cbt$beta + 1.96 * robust_results_cbt$SE,
  p_value = format.pval(robust_results_cbt$p_Satt, digits = 3, eps = 0.001)
)

print(robust_ci_full)
```

```{r}
# Extract for comparison table
robust_coef_cbt <- robust_results_cbt["exp_session", ]

# Create comparison table
comparison_se_cbt <- data.frame(
  Effect = "exp_session",
  Original_Est = round(summary(m2_cbt)$coefficients["exp_session", "Estimate"], 5),
  Original_SE = round(summary(m2_cbt)$coefficients["exp_session", "Std. Error"], 5),
  Original_p = format.pval(summary(m2_cbt)$coefficients["exp_session", "Pr(>|t|)"], 
                          digits = 3, eps = 0.001),
  Robust_Est = round(robust_coef_cbt$beta, 5),
  Robust_SE = round(robust_coef_cbt$SE, 5),
  Robust_p = format.pval(robust_coef_cbt$p_Satt, digits = 3, eps = 0.001)
)

# Calculate changes
comparison_se_cbt$Delta_SE <- round(comparison_se_cbt$Robust_SE - comparison_se_cbt$Original_SE, 5)
comparison_se_cbt$Delta_p <- round(as.numeric(sub("<", "", comparison_se_cbt$Robust_p)) - 
                                   as.numeric(sub("<", "", comparison_se_cbt$Original_p)), 5)

kable(comparison_se_cbt[, 1:7],
      row.names = FALSE,
      col.names = c("Effect", "Estimate", "SE", "p-value", 
                    "Estimate", "SE", "p-value"),
      caption = "Comparison: Original vs. Robust Standard Errors (m2_cbt)",
      align = c('l', 'r', 'r', 'r', 'r', 'r', 'r')) %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE, bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover")) %>%
  add_header_above(c(" " = 1, "Original Model" = 3, "Robust SEs (CR2)" = 3))
```

Interpretation Sensitivity 2: When accounting for non-linearity (Shaprio Wilk Test), using cluster-robust standard errors (CR2 adjustment), the main effect of experimental session became insignificant (β=0.019, SE=0.013, p=0.211). The robust standard error (0.013) was 61% larger than the original SE (0.008), reflecting the reduced effective sample size (df=6.4 vs. 59.5) when properly accounting for within-participant clustering. Due to the fact that the experimental session effect became insignificant in all sensitivity analyses performed so far, it needs to be treated with extreme caution.

### Sensitivity Analysis: Exclusion of Influential Observations

**Context:** Three observations were identified as influential based on Cook's distance (threshold: 4/n = 0.0597). To assess whether these observations drive the session effect, the model was refitted excluding these cases.

```{r}
# Identify influential observations (from earlier analysis)
infl_m2_cbt <- influence(m2_cbt, obs = TRUE)
cooks_d_cbt <- cooks.distance(infl_m2_cbt)
threshold_cbt <- 4/nrow(cbt_lmm)

influential_idx_cbt <- which(cooks_d_cbt > threshold_cbt)

cat("Number of influential observations:", length(influential_idx_cbt), "\n")
cat("Percentage of data:", round(length(influential_idx_cbt)/nrow(cbt_lmm)*100, 1), "%\n\n")

# Display influential observations
cat("Influential observations:\n")
print(cbt_lmm[influential_idx_cbt, c("participant_id", "exp_session", "cbt_intervention")])
```

```{r}
# Create dataset without influential observations
cbt_lmm_robust <- cbt_lmm[-influential_idx_cbt, ]

cat("\nOriginal dataset: n =", nrow(cbt_lmm), "observations\n")
cat("Robust dataset: n =", nrow(cbt_lmm_robust), "observations\n")
cat("Excluded:", nrow(cbt_lmm) - nrow(cbt_lmm_robust), "observations\n")
```

```{r}
# Refit primary model without influential observations
m2_cbt_robust <- lmer(
  cbt_intervention ~ exp_session + (1 | participant_id),
  data = cbt_lmm_robust,
  REML = FALSE
)

summary(m2_cbt_robust)

# Wald Confidence Intervals
ci_m2_robust <- confint(m2_cbt_robust, method = "Wald")
print(ci_m2_robust)
```

Interpretation Sensitivity 3: Excluding 3 influential observations (P01 Session 3, P10 Session 3, P03 Session 10) did not change results massively (β=0.023, p=0.002). Therefore conclusions drawn from model m2 were robust to the exclusion of those identified three influential observations.

### Primary Model m2 Results with Benjamini-Hochberg Correction

**Context:** Although the primary model (m2_cbt) contains only a single fixed effect predictor (exp_session), we apply the Benjamini-Hochberg correction for consistency with the analysis framework and to demonstrate that the finding is not affected by multiple comparison adjustment.

```{r}
# Extract coefficients
m2_cbt_coef <- summary(m2_cbt)$coefficients
m2_cbt_fixed <- rownames(m2_cbt_coef)[rownames(m2_cbt_coef) != "(Intercept)"]

# Extract raw p-values
m2_cbt_p_raw <- m2_cbt_coef[m2_cbt_fixed, "Pr(>|t|)"]

# Apply Benjamini-Hochberg correction
m2_cbt_p_bh <- p.adjust(m2_cbt_p_raw, method = "BH")

# Create results table
m2_cbt_results <- data.frame(
  Effect = m2_cbt_fixed,
  Estimate = round(m2_cbt_coef[m2_cbt_fixed, "Estimate"], 5),
  SE = round(m2_cbt_coef[m2_cbt_fixed, "Std. Error"], 5),
  t = round(m2_cbt_coef[m2_cbt_fixed, "t value"], 3),
  df = round(m2_cbt_coef[m2_cbt_fixed, "df"], 1),
  p_raw = format.pval(m2_cbt_p_raw, digits = 3, eps = 0.001),
  p_BH = format.pval(m2_cbt_p_bh, digits = 3, eps = 0.001)
)

# Calculate cumulative effect over 10 sessions
baseline_cbt <- fixef(m2_cbt)["(Intercept)"]
sessions_range <- max(cbt_lmm$exp_session) - min(cbt_lmm$exp_session)

m2_cbt_results <- m2_cbt_results %>%
  mutate(
    Cumulative_10sessions = round(Estimate * sessions_range, 3),
    Percent_baseline = round((Cumulative_10sessions / baseline_cbt) * 100, 2)
  )

kable(m2_cbt_results, 
      caption = "CBT Model (m2_cbt): Fixed Effects with Benjamini-Hochberg Correction",
      col.names = c("Effect", "Estimate\n(°C/session)", "SE", "t", "df", 
                    "p (raw)", "p (BH)", "Cumulative\nΔ (10 sessions)", "% of\nbaseline"),
      align = c('l', 'r', 'r', 'r', 'r', 'r', 'r', 'r', 'r')) %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE, bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"))
```

## Exploratory Analyses

### Exploratory Analysis 1a: Random Slopes for Light_Lag0

**Rationale:** The primary models (m1a-m1c) assumed that light effects are identical across all participants (fixed slopes). This exploratory analysis tests whether participants vary in their response to current-day light exposure by fitting random slopes for Light_Lag0.

```{r}
# Fit model with random slopes for Light_Lag0
m1c_cbt_rs_lag0 <- lmer(
  cbt_intervention ~ Light_Lag0_num + Light_Lag1_num + Light_Lag2_num + exp_session +
    (1 + Light_Lag0_num | participant_id),
  data = cbt_lmm, 
  REML = FALSE, 
  control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa")
)

summary(m1c_cbt_rs_lag0)

# Wald Confidence Intervals
ci_m1c_cbt_rs_lag0 <- confint(m1c_cbt_rs_lag0, method = "Wald")
print(ci_m1c_cbt_rs_lag0)
```

Interpretation Exploratory Analysis 1a random slopes for Lag 0: Model is overparameterised. There is a perfect correlation between the random slope and the random intercept. This might be due to too little variation among the individuals, too low sample size, too complex model structure with respect to the data available.

### Exploratory Analysis 1b: Random Slopes for Session Effect

**Rationale:** The primary model (m2_cbt) assumed that the temporal trajectory across sessions is identical for all participants (fixed slope). This exploratory analysis tests whether participants vary in their temporal dynamics by fitting random slopes for the session effect.

```{r}
# Fit model with random slopes for exp_session
m2_cbt_rs <- lmer(
  cbt_intervention ~ exp_session + (1 + exp_session | participant_id),
  data = cbt_lmm, 
  REML = FALSE, 
  control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa")
)

summary(m2_cbt_rs)

# Wald Confidence Intervals
ci_m2_cbt_rs <- confint(m2_cbt_rs, method = "Wald")
print(ci_m2_cbt_rs)
```

Interpretation Exploratory 1a: There is moderate between individual variation in baseline cbt values (SD=0.294); however the variance of the slope for the experimental session effect is quite small (SD=0.028), indicating that participants follow similar temporal trajectories. Furthermore, a negative correlation of -0.63 suggests that subjects with higher baseline cbt values have less steep increases in cbt across experimental sessions. The fixed effect of experimental session is not significant (β=0.019, SE=0.012, p=0.162).

### Exploratory Analysis 2a: Age and Sex Moderation

**Rationale:** To test whether the session effect on core body temperature is moderated by biological sex or age, interactions between exp_session and demographic variables were examined.

```{r}
# Center age
cbt_lmm <- cbt_lmm %>%
  mutate(age_c = age - mean(age, na.rm = TRUE))

# Moderation model with exp_session interactions
m2_cbt_moderation <- lmer(
  cbt_intervention ~ 
    exp_session +
    sex + age_c + 
    exp_session:sex + exp_session:age_c +
    (1 | participant_id),
  data = cbt_lmm,
  REML = FALSE
)

summary(m2_cbt_moderation)

# Wald Confidence Intervals
ci_m2_cbt_moderation <- confint(m2_cbt_moderation, method = "Wald")
print(ci_m2_cbt_moderation)
```

Interpretation Exploratory 2a (Age, Sex Moderation): No significant effects were found for experimental session (β=0.023, p=0.053), biological sex (male compared to female as reference category; β=-0.26, p=0.216), age (centered) (β=0.009, p=0.727), or the interactions between sex and session (β=-0.004, p=0.754) and age and session (β=-0.002, p=0.462).

### Exploratory Analysis 2b: Age and Sex Moderation of Light Effects

**Rationale:** To test whether the effects of evening light exposure on core body temperature are moderated by biological sex or age.

```{r}
# Center age
cbt_lmm <- cbt_lmm %>%
  mutate(age_c = age - mean(age, na.rm = TRUE))

# Moderation model with light interactions
m1c_cbt_moderation_light <- lmer(
  cbt_intervention ~ 
    Light_Lag0_num + Light_Lag1_num + Light_Lag2_num +
    sex + age_c + 
    Light_Lag0_num:sex + Light_Lag0_num:age_c +
    Light_Lag1_num:sex + Light_Lag1_num:age_c +
    Light_Lag2_num:sex + Light_Lag2_num:age_c +
    (1 | participant_id),
  data = cbt_lmm,
  REML = FALSE
)

summary(m1c_cbt_moderation_light)

# Wald Confidence Intervals
ci_m1c_cbt_moderation_light <- confint(m1c_cbt_moderation_light, method = "Wald")
print(ci_m1c_cbt_moderation_light)
```

Interpretation Exploratory 2b (Age, Sex Moderation for Light Lags): In this model a marginal trend for an increase in CBT with current evening\`s bright light exposure was observed (β= 0.104, p=0.058) and of light exposure 3 evenings before (β= 0.094, p=0.087).However all other effects were non-significant, including Light Lag 1 (β=-0.018, p=0.747), biological sex (male vs. female reference, β=-0.218, p=0.226), and age (centered; β=0.007, p=0.764). None of the six interactions (3 Light-Lags × Sex + 3 Light-Lags × Age) reached significance (all p \> 0.10), suggesting that light effects on CBT are not moderated by sex or age.

### Exploratory Analysis 3: BMI Effects on Core Body Temperature

**Rationale:** Body Mass Index (BMI) affects thermoregulation through multiple mechanisms including metabolic rate, insulation, and surface-area-to-volume ratio. This exploratory analysis tests whether BMI is associated with baseline core body temperature and/or modulates temporal dynamics.

#### Step 1: BMI Main Effect (Baseline Model)

```{r}
# Center BMI
cbt_lmm <- cbt_lmm %>%
  mutate(bmi_c = bmi - mean(bmi, na.rm = TRUE))

# Model 1: BMI only
m_bmi_simple <- lmer(
  cbt_intervention ~ bmi_c + (1 | participant_id),
  data = cbt_lmm,
  REML = FALSE
)

summary(m_bmi_simple)

# Wald Confidence Intervals
ci_m_bmi_simple <- confint(m_bmi_simple, method = "Wald")
print(ci_m_bmi_simple)
```

Interpretation Exploratory 3 (BMI only): no significant effect of Body Mass Index on average CBT values was found (centered; β=0.015; p=0.584).

#### Step 2: BMI + Session Effect

```{r}
# Model 2: BMI + exp_session
m_bmi_session <- lmer(
  cbt_intervention ~ exp_session + bmi_c + (1 | participant_id),
  data = cbt_lmm,
  REML = FALSE
)

summary(m_bmi_session)

# Wald Confidence Intervals
ci_m_bmi_session <- confint(m_bmi_session, method = "Wald")
print(ci_m_bmi_session)
```

Interpretation Exploratory 3 (BMI + experimental Session): When including BMI centered into the model (β=0.013, p=0.642), the main effect of experimental session on CBT values remained significant (β=0.019, p=0.030).

### Exploratory Analysis 4: Light Lag Interactions

**Rationale:** To test whether the effects of evening light exposure on different days interact synergistically or antagonistically, all two-way interactions between Lag 0, Lag 1, and Lag 2 were investigated.

```{r}
m1c_cbt_interactions <- lmer(
  cbt_intervention ~ 
    Light_Lag0_num * Light_Lag1_num + 
    Light_Lag0_num * Light_Lag2_num +
    Light_Lag1_num * Light_Lag2_num +
    (1 | participant_id),
  data = cbt_lmm,
  REML = FALSE
)

summary(m1c_cbt_interactions)

# Wald Confidence Intervals
ci_m1c_cbt_interactions <- confint(m1c_cbt_interactions, method = "Wald")
print(ci_m1c_cbt_interactions)
```

Interpretation Exploratory 4 (Light Lag Interactions): All main effects of light as well as all three two-way interactions between the different Light Lag predictors were not statistically significant (p\>0.1), suggesting no synergistic or antagonistic effects between light exposures on consecutive days.

# Exploratory 5: CBT Persistence Analysis

## Rationale

The persistence analysis for CBT addresses the question: Does the number of consecutive days of the same light condition (run length) modulate CBT responses? This tests whether:

-   **Dim nights**: Multiple consecutive dim evenings produce cumulative effects on CBT
-   **Bright nights**: Multiple consecutive bright evenings produce cumulative effects on CBT

Key distinction from lag analysis: - **Lag analysis**: Tests whether Day\[t-1\], Day\[t-2\] each add independent effects - **Persistence analysis**: Tests whether being on the 1st vs. 2nd vs. 3rd+ consecutive day of the same condition matters

## Dataset Preparation

```{r}
participant_list <- c("P01", "P02", "P03", "P04", "P05", "P06", "P09", "P10")

cbt_persistence <- map_dfr(participant_list, ~{
  df <- cbt %>% 
    filter(id == .x) %>%
    # Extract last 2 digits from session (e.g., "101" -> 01, "111" -> 11)
    mutate(exp_session = as.integer(substr(session, nchar(session)-1, nchar(session)))) %>%
    filter(!is.na(cbt_intervention)) %>%
    # Aggregate by session: take mean cbt_intervention per session
    group_by(id, exp_session) %>%
    summarise(cbt_intervention = mean(cbt_intervention, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
    rename(participant_id = id)
  
  # Get light pattern
  pattern_vec <- light_patterns[[.x]]
  
  if (.x == "P10") {
    # For P10: create indices for sessions excluding position 5
    # P10 has 13 positions total, but position 5 is excluded
    # Sessions are: 1,2,3,4,6,7,8,9,10,11,12,13
    valid_sessions <- c(1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13)
    light_df <- tibble(
      exp_session = valid_sessions, 
      Light_Lag0 = pattern_vec
    )
  } else {
    light_df <- tibble(
      exp_session = seq_along(pattern_vec), 
      Light_Lag0 = pattern_vec
    )
  }
  
  df %>% left_join(light_df, by = "exp_session")
})

# Add demographics 
cbt_persistence <- cbt_persistence %>%
  left_join(participant_demographics_cbt, by = "participant_id") %>%
  filter(!is.na(Light_Lag0)) %>%
  filter(!(participant_id == "P10" & exp_session == 5)) %>%
  filter(participant_id != "P07") %>%  # Exclude P07
  arrange(participant_id, exp_session) %>%
  group_by(participant_id) %>%
  mutate(
    condition_change = Light_Lag0 != lag(Light_Lag0, default = "CHANGE"),
    run_id = cumsum(condition_change),
    run_length = ave(run_id, run_id, FUN = seq_along),
    run_length_dim = ifelse(Light_Lag0 == "D", run_length, NA),
    run_length_bright = ifelse(Light_Lag0 == "B", run_length, NA),
    Light_Lag0_num = ifelse(Light_Lag0 == "D", 0, 1)
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    run_category_dim = factor(case_when(
      run_length_dim == 1 ~ "First",
      run_length_dim == 2 ~ "Second",
      run_length_dim >= 3 ~ "Third"
    ), levels = c("First", "Second", "Third")),
    run_category_bright = factor(case_when(
      run_length_bright == 1 ~ "First",
      run_length_bright == 2 ~ "Second",
      run_length_bright >= 3 ~ "Third"
    ), levels = c("First", "Second", "Third"))
  ) %>%
  select(participant_id, exp_session, cbt_intervention, Light_Lag0, Light_Lag0_num,
         run_length, run_length_dim, run_length_bright, 
         run_category_dim, run_category_bright, sex, age, bmi)
```

## Model 1: Linear Persistence Models, Dim Evenings

```{r}
cbt_persistence_dim <- cbt_persistence %>% filter(!is.na(run_length_dim))

model_persistence_dim_numeric <- lmer(
  cbt_intervention ~ run_length_dim + (1 | participant_id),
  data = cbt_persistence_dim,
  REML = FALSE
)

summary(model_persistence_dim_numeric)

# Wald Confidence Intervals
ci_model_persistence_dim_numeric <- confint(model_persistence_dim_numeric, method = "Wald")
print(ci_model_persistence_dim_numeric)

cbt_persistence_dim_no_s1 <- cbt_persistence %>% filter(!is.na(run_length_dim), exp_session > 1)

model_persistence_dim_no_s1 <- lmer(
  cbt_intervention ~ run_length_dim + (1 | participant_id),
  data = cbt_persistence_dim_no_s1,
  REML = FALSE
)

summary(model_persistence_dim_no_s1)

# Wald Confidence Intervals
ci_model_persistence_dim_no_s1 <- confint(model_persistence_dim_no_s1, method = "Wald")
print(ci_model_persistence_dim_no_s1)
```

Interpretation Exploratory 4 Persistence, Linear, Dim: To test whether consecutive dim light evenings produce cumulative effects on average core body temperature during the light intervention window, the linear relationship between run length (number of consecutive dim evenings) and CBT was examined. Two models were fitted, whilst the first model includes all observations, the second model excludes Session 1, as there is no controlled light exposure on the previous day, which might influence results.

Including Session 1 for dim evening analysis did not find a linear effect of consecutive dim evenings for average core body temperature (β=-0.01902, p=0.668)

Excluding Session 1 for dim evening analysis did not find a linear effect of consecutive dim evenings for average core body temperature (β=-0.05374, p=0.242)

The negative (non-significant) coefficients suggest a slight decrease in mean core body temperature for consecutive dim light evening exposure, however this trend is not statistically significant.

As the first evening light exposure was dim for all participants, the analysis including and excluding session 1 are the same.

No statistically significant linear persistence effect was found for consecutive bright evenings (β=0.01178, p=0.711).

## Model 2: Categorical Persistence Models, Dim Evenings

```{r}
cbt_persistence_dim <- cbt_persistence %>% filter(!is.na(run_category_dim))

  cbt_intervention ~ run_category_dim + (1 | participant_id),

  REML = FALSE
)

summary(model_persistence_dim_categorical)

# Wald Confidence Intervals

print(ci_model_persistence_dim_categorical)

cbt_persistence_dim_no_s1 <- cbt_persistence %>% filter(!is.na(run_category_dim), exp_session > 1)

model_persistence_dim_categorical_no_s1 <- lmer(
  cbt_intervention ~ run_category_dim + (1 | participant_id),
  data = cbt_persistence_dim_no_s1,
  REML = FALSE
)

summary(model_persistence_dim_categorical_no_s1)

# Wald Confidence Intervals
ci_model_persistence_dim_categorical_no_s1  <- confint(model_persistence_dim_categorical_no_s1, method = "Wald")
print(ci_model_persistence_dim_categorical_no_s1)
```

Interpretation Exploratory 4 Persistence, Categorical, Dim:

In order to examine potential non-linear patterns of cumulative dim light exposure on mean core body temperature, a model was fitted using the categories second (2nd day cumulative dim light exposure) and third (3rd day cumulative dim light exposure) compared to the first dim night (reference category) to predict mean core body temperature values during the light intervention window. As in the linear persistence analysis, two models (first with, second without first experimental session) were fitted.

Including Session 1 for dim evening analysis did not find non-linear effects of consecutive dim evenings for CBT values: Second (β=0.005159, p=0.949), Third (β=-0.047849, p=0.606).

Excluding Session 1 for dim evening analysis did not find non-linear effects of consecutive dim evenings for CBT values: Second (β=-0.05645, p=0.495), Third (β=-0.10670, p=0.257).

These results are in alignment with the dim, linear analysis, indicating neither linear nor non-linear effects of consecutive evening dim light exposure on core body temperature.

# Exploratory Analysis 6: Climate Chamber Data

An exploratory model including the temperature ddata from the climate chamber during the intervention window will be used to identify a potential impact of the climate temperature on core body temperature values. Despite efforts to keep the chamber at a constant temperature throughout and across sessions, some deviations happened, hence this analysis examines the robustness of findings to the inclusion of the climate chmaber data.

```{r process-group1}
# Filter data
group1_dates <- seq(as.Date("2025-06-16"), by = "day", length.out = 11)
climate_group1_all <- climate_lab %>%
  filter(
    as.Date(unix_converted) %in% group1_dates,
    hour(unix_converted) == 21 & minute(unix_converted) >= 30 |
    hour(unix_converted) == 22 |
    hour(unix_converted) == 23 & minute(unix_converted) == 0
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    unix_converted = floor_date(unix_converted, unit = "minute"),
    temp_felt = (tg + tdb) / 2
  )

# Check missing data
gaps <- climate_group1_all %>%
  arrange(unix_converted) %>%
  group_by(as.Date(unix_converted)) %>%
  mutate(time_diff = as.numeric(difftime(unix_converted, lag(unix_converted), units = "mins"))) %>%
  filter(time_diff > 1) %>%
  ungroup()

cat("Total obs:", nrow(climate_group1_all), "| Gaps > 1 min:", nrow(gaps), "\n\n")
table(as.Date(climate_group1_all$unix_converted))

# Daily average
temp_felt_daily <- climate_group1_all %>%
  group_by(date_only = as.Date(unix_converted)) %>%
  summarise(temp_felt_mean = mean(temp_felt, na.rm = TRUE), n_obs = n())
print(temp_felt_daily)
```

## Add the climate temperature variable to the cbt_lmm dataset

```{r clean-and-rejoin-temperature}
# Remove temperature columns
cbt_lmm <- cbt_lmm %>%
  select(-contains("temp_felt_mean"), -contains("date_only"))

# Create temperature lookup
temp_lookup <- bind_rows(
  temp_felt_daily %>% mutate(group = 1, participants = list(c("P01", "P02", "P03"))),
  temp_felt_daily_group2 %>% mutate(group = 2, participants = list(c("P04", "P05"))),
  temp_felt_daily_group3 %>% mutate(group = 3, participants = list(c("P06", "P07", "P09"))),
  temp_felt_daily_group4 %>% mutate(group = 4, participants = list(c("P10")))
) %>%
  unnest(participants) %>%
  group_by(participants, group) %>%
  mutate(exp_session = row_number()) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(participant_id = participants, exp_session, temp_felt_mean, date_only)

# Join temperature data
cbt_lmm <- cbt_lmm %>%
  left_join(temp_lookup, by = c("participant_id", "exp_session"))

# Check result
cbt_lmm %>% 
  filter(participant_id == "P01", exp_session == 3) %>%
  select(participant_id, exp_session, cbt_intervention, temp_felt_mean, date_only)
```

## Exploratory 6: Fit LMM with the sensed temperature as fixed effect

```{r exploratory-lmm-temperature}
# Model 1 m_temp: Temperature as predictor
m_temp <- lmer(
  cbt_intervention ~ temp_felt_mean + (1 | participant_id),
  data = cbt_lmm,
  REML = FALSE
)

summary(m_temp)

# Wald Confidence Intervals
ci_m_temp <- confint(m_temp, method = "Wald")
print(ci_m_temp)

# Model 2: Session + Temperature
m_session_temp <- lmer(
  cbt_intervention ~ exp_session + temp_felt_mean + (1 | participant_id),
  data = cbt_lmm,
  REML = FALSE
)

summary(m_session_temp)

# Wald Confidence Intervals
ci_m_session_temp <- confint(m_session_temp, method = "Wald")
print(ci_m_session_temp)

# Model 3: Lag 0 + Temperature 
m_lag0_temp <- lmer(
  cbt_intervention ~ Light_Lag0_num + temp_felt_mean + (1 | participant_id),
  data = cbt_lmm,
  REML = FALSE
)

summary(m_lag0_temp)

# Wald Confidence Intervals
ci_m_lag0_temp <- confint(m_lag0_temp, method = "Wald")
print(ci_m_lag0_temp)

# Model 4: Lag 1 + Temperature 
m_lag1_temp <- lmer(
  cbt_intervention ~ Light_Lag1_num + temp_felt_mean + (1 | participant_id),
  data = cbt_lmm,
  REML = FALSE
)

summary(m_lag1_temp)

# Wald Confidence Intervals
ci_m_lag1_temp <- confint(m_lag1_temp, method = "Wald")
print(ci_m_lag1_temp)

# Model 5: Lag 2 + Temperature 
m_lag2_temp <- lmer(
  cbt_intervention ~ Light_Lag2_num + temp_felt_mean + (1 | participant_id),
  data = cbt_lmm,
  REML = FALSE
)

summary(m_lag2_temp)

# Wald Confidence Intervals
ci_m_lag2_temp <- confint(m_lag2_temp, method = "Wald")
print(ci_m_lag2_temp)
```

Interpretation Exploratory 6 (Sensed Temperature in the Climate Chamber during the Intervention Window):

-   Model 1 (temperature as fixed effect only): Mean sensed temperature during the intervention window in the climate chamber did not have a statistically significant effect on CBT values (β= 0.05421, p=0.294).

-   Model 2 (temperature + experimental session as fixed effects): While controlling for laboratory temperature (β=0.041826, p=0.4023), the main effect of experimental session on CBT values remained statistically significant (β=0.017830, p=0.0361).

-   Model 3 (temperature + Light Lag 0): No significant effects were observed for temperature (β=0.03817, p=0.516) or current evening light exposure (β=0.02836, p=0.577) on CBT values.

-   Model 4 (temperature + Light Lag 1): No significant effects were observed for temperature (β=0.05841, p=0.261) or prior evening light exposure (β=0.02819, p=0.529).

-   Model 5 (temperature + Light Lag 2): No significant effects were observed for temperature (β=0.06158, p=0.227), though evening light exposure two days prior showed a marginal trend (β=0.06723, p=0.129) on CBT values.

As a summary, no statistically significant effects of sensed temperature within the climate chamber were observed. This suggests that efforts to maintain temperature at a controlled, constant level were successful, and that temperature did not confound the relationships between experimental session, light exposure, and CBT.

### Statistical Analysis Summary Table

```{r cbt-model-comparison-overview}
# Helper functions to extract coefficients from LMM
get_coef_lmm <- function(model, coef_name) {
  coefs <- summary(model)$coefficients
  if (coef_name %in% rownames(coefs)) {
    return(coefs[coef_name, "Estimate"])
  } else {
    return(NA)
  }
}

get_p_lmm <- function(model, coef_name) {
  coefs <- summary(model)$coefficients
  if (coef_name %in% rownames(coefs)) {
    return(coefs[coef_name, "Pr(>|t|)"])
  } else {
    return(NA)
  }
}

# Create extended comparison table for CBT
model_comparison_cbt <- data.frame(
  Model = c(
    "m0 (Baseline)",
    "m1a (Lag 0)",
    "m1b (Lag 0+1)",

      caption = "Model Comparison: All Tested Models for Core Body Temperature (CBT)",
      align = c('l', 'l', 'c', 'c', 'c', 'c', 'c', 'c', 'l'),
      col.names = c("Model", "Description", "npar", "N", "AIC", "BIC", 
                    "β Main", "p Main", "Status")) %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE, bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover")) %>%
  row_spec(5, bold = TRUE, background = "#D6EAF8") %>%
  pack_rows("Primary Model Selection (n=67)", 1, 6) %>%
  pack_rows("Sensitivity Analyses", 7, 9) %>%
  pack_rows("Exploratory Analyses", 10, 19)
```

```{r cbt-final-model-summary}
# Extract fixed effects from m2_cbt
m2_cbt_coef <- summary(m2_cbt)$coefficients

# Create results table
m2_cbt_results <- data.frame(
  Effect = c("exp_session"),
  Beta = round(m2_cbt_coef["exp_session", "Estimate"], 3),
  SE = round(m2_cbt_coef["exp_session", "Std. Error"], 3),
  t = round(m2_cbt_coef["exp_session", "t value"], 3),
  p = format.pval(m2_cbt_coef["exp_session", "Pr(>|t|)"], 
                  digits = 3, eps = 0.001),
  Effect_size = paste0("+", round(m2_cbt_coef["exp_session", "Estimate"], 3), 
                       " °C/session")
)

kable(m2_cbt_results, 
      col.names = c("Effect", "β (°C)", "SE", "t", "p", "Effect Size"),
      caption = "Final Model (m2_cbt): Fixed Effects for Experimental Session") %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE, bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"))
```

```{r cbt-variance-components}
# Variance components for m2_cbt
vc_final_cbt <- as.data.frame(VarCorr(m2_cbt))

cat("\n**Variance Components (m2_cbt):**\n")
cat("Between-participant (Random Intercept):", round(vc_final_cbt$vcov[1], 3), "\n")
cat("Within-participant (Residual):", round(vc_final_cbt$vcov[2], 3), "\n\n")

# Calculate ICC
icc_final_cbt <- vc_final_cbt$vcov[1] / (vc_final_cbt$vcov[1] + vc_final_cbt$vcov[2])
cat("ICC (Intraclass Correlation):", round(icc_final_cbt, 3), 
    paste0("(", round(icc_final_cbt * 100, 1), "% of variance between participants)"), "\n\n")

cat("**Model Fit:**\n")
cat("AIC:", round(AIC(m2_cbt), 1), "| BIC:", round(BIC(m2_cbt), 1), "\n")
cat("N obs:", nrow(cbt_lmm), "| N participants:", 
    length(unique(cbt_lmm$participant_id)), "\n")
cat("Family: Gaussian (identity link)\n\n")
```

```{r}
# Labels with bold second letter

)

# Labels with bold third letter

  "DDD" = expression("DD"*bold("D")),

)

# Colors based on third letter
triplet_colors <- c(
  "DDD" = "#4A90E2", "BDD" = "#4A90E2", "DBD" = "#4A90E2", "BBD" = "#4A90E2",
  "DDB" = "#F5A623", "BDB" = "#F5A623", "DBB" = "#F5A623", "BBB" = "#F5A623"
)

# Compute shared y-axis range across all four datasets
all_values <- c(
  df_plot_cbt_noP07$mean_cbt,
  df_plot_cbt_int_noP07$mean_cbt_int,
  df_plot_cbt_triplet_noP07$mean_cbt,
  df_plot_cbt_triplet_int_noP07$mean_cbt_int
)
y_min <- floor(min(all_values, na.rm = TRUE) * 10) / 10
y_max <- ceiling(max(all_values, na.rm = TRUE) * 10) / 10
y_breaks <- pretty(c(y_min, y_max), n = 6)

# --- Plot 1: Doublet 5h ---
p1 <- ggplot(df_plot_cbt_noP07, aes(x = doublet, y = mean_cbt)) +
  geom_boxplot(aes(fill = doublet), outlier.shape = NA, width = 0.6, linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_point(position = position_jitter(width = 0.15, seed = 42),
             size = 2.5, alpha = 0.7, shape = 16) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = doublet_colors) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = doublet_labels) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(y_min, y_max), breaks = y_breaks) +
  labs(
    title = "Doublets \u2013 5-h exposure",
    x = "Doublet",
    y = "Mean Core Body Temperature (\u00b0C)"
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    aspect.ratio = 1,
    plot.title = element_text(size = 16, hjust = 0),
    axis.text = element_text(color = "black", size = 13),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 14),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(color = "grey90", linewidth = 0.3),
    legend.position = "none"
  )

# --- Plot 2: Doublet 1.5h ---
p2 <- ggplot(df_plot_cbt_int_noP07, aes(x = doublet, y = mean_cbt_int)) +
```
